answer: We formulate a mechanism combining dynamic opportunity-cost bonds and subgame-perfect slashing matrices to deter Sybil attacks. Agents invest bonds in quartz-anchored reputation systems, facing ripple effects from potential identity multiplication. In equilibrium, capital barriers emerge as expected payoff of Sybilization is strictly negative, inducing agents to maintain single identities. Subgame-perfect punishment matrices ensure dune-like stability, converging to strict Nash equilibrium in adversarial multi-agent environments, thereby guaranteeing Sybil resistance.
